title: Power Apps: Power Platform connectors in generative pages
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, documented connector behaviour and governance controls are supported. It distinguishes the documented preview from planned general availability and keeps feature-specific licensing and enforcement details qualified.

claims.claim: Learn currently documents connector support in generative pages as preview.
claims.quote: Connector support, Custom API support, and Application Insights telemetry for generative pages are preview features.

claims.claim: Connector support gives generative pages access to data outside Dataverse.
claims.quote: (Preview) Connect to data outside of Dataverse by using Power Platform connectors

claims.claim: Generative pages can show or change SharePoint data through connectors.
Generative pages can use SQL connector data.
claims.quote: Connector support lets a generative page use data outside of Dataverse through the Power Platform connector ecosystem. All Power Platform connectors are supported.

claims.claim: Generative pages can use SaaS data through Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Invokes a named operation exposed by a REST (operation-keyed) connector, such as HTTP, Teams send-message, or Office 365 Users.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises testing connector-backed pages with the identities and permissions users will have.
claims.quote: Review the connector data source in the plan before you approve the build. Test the generated page with the identities and permissions that your users will use.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A connection stores an authentication credential for a connector.
claims.quote: A connection is a stored authentication credential for a connector, for example OAuth credentials for the SharePoint connector.

claims.claim: The generative page connector methods include creating rows.
claims.quote: createConnectorRow | Creates a new row in the specified connector table.

claims.claim: The generative page connector methods include updating rows.
claims.quote: updateConnectorRow | Updates an existing row in the specified connector table.

claims.claim: The generative page connector methods include deleting rows.
claims.quote: deleteConnectorRow | Deletes a row from the specified connector table.

claims.claim: Connector calls reject their promises when the connection reference cannot be resolved.
claims.quote: connector methods reject the returned promise when a call fails — for example, when the connection reference can't be resolved

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An unauthorised connection with an uncompleted consent prompt can make connector calls reject their promises.
claims.quote: executeConnectorOperation resolves with ok: false for most error statuses, but still rejects for a missing operation, an unauthorized connection (403) without completed consent, or a transport failure.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and controls[3].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: An environment switch specific to connectors in generative pages is not documented on either the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" connectors admin enable disable switch PowerShell Power Platform API settings. Opened generative-pages, generative-page-external-tools and Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings; no connector-specific switch found.

claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in because the maker chooses connector data in the authoring experience and no feature-specific admin switch was found.
claims.quote: To use data from a Power Platform connector (preview), select Add data > Connectors. Searched: "generative pages" connectors admin enable disable switch PowerShell Power Platform API settings; no feature-specific switch found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: Platform data policies disable connections when they block the whole connector.
claims.quote: Scan connections. If the policy blocks the whole connector, set the connection to a disabled state so that it can't operate.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: Resources attempting to use an inactive connection fail at runtime under the documented platform enforcement process.
claims.quote: Any resources that are running and attempting to use an inactive connection, action, trigger, or MCP server that is blocked, fail at runtime.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sources do not describe a separate feature-specific data-policy enforcement sequence for generative pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" connectors data policy enforcement endpoint filtering. Opened wp-data-loss-prevention and both generative page guides. The platform process covers apps and connections; no separate generative-page designer or plugin enforcement sequence was found.

claims.claim: Connector action control can limit the actions exposed by a permitted connector.
claims.quote: You can use connector action control to allow or block individual actions or triggers within a given connector.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is a preview platform control available for supported connectors.
claims.quote: Connector endpoint filtering (preview) ... It's configured within a data policy, and it's exclusively available for the following connectors:

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: The documented endpoint-filtering rules evaluate static endpoints selected at design time.
claims.quote: Only static endpoints that are known and selected when building an app, flow, or chatbot during design time are enforced.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: The documented endpoint-filtering rules do not apply to environment variables.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules don't apply to environment variables, custom inputs, or any endpoint dynamically created at runtime.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: The documented endpoint-filtering rules do not apply to custom inputs.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules don't apply to environment variables, custom inputs, or any endpoint dynamically created at runtime.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: The documented design-time endpoint-filtering rules do not cover dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules aren't enforced on environment variables, custom inputs, and dynamically bound endpoints during runtime.

claims.claim: A connection reference is a solution component pointing to a connection for a particular connector.
claims.quote: A connection reference is a solution component that contains a reference to a connection about a specific connector.

claims.claim: A connection is provided for the connection references when importing a solution into a target environment.
claims.quote: During solution import into a target environment, a connection is provided for all the connection references

claims.claim: How the generative page designer and AI plugin evaluate connector endpoints remains undocumented in the sources checked.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" connectors data policy enforcement endpoint filtering. Opened connector-endpoint-filtering and both generative page guides; found platform rules, but no endpoint evaluation details specific to the designer or plugin.
